title: Algebra-linear test-resolution models restrict naturally to the base derived tensor
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $K^\bullet$ any unbounded complex of $A$-modules, $N$ an $R$-module, and $\epsilon:P^\bullet\to N[0]$ a K-flat resolution over $R$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Use the unbounded derived categories and their localization functors $Q_R,Q_A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Give $C(K,P)=\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)$ the $A$-action on the $K$ factor and the signed direct-sum total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This is an $A$-complex, and there is an isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$\eta_{K,\epsilon}:Q_R(\operatorname{Res}_R C(K,P))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(\operatorname{Res}_R K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(N[0]).$$
These isomorphisms can be chosen simultaneously with the following compatibility: for every $A$-linear chain map $f:K\to K'$, $R$-linear module map $g:N\to N'$, and $R$-linear chain map $h:P\to P'$ between K-flat resolutions satisfying $\epsilon'h=g[0]\epsilon$, the square with top and bottom $\eta_{K,\epsilon},\eta_{K',\epsilon'}$, left arrow $Q_R(\operatorname{Res}_R\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes h))$ and right arrow $Q_R(\operatorname{Res}_R f)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(g[0])$ commutes. In particular, multiplication by any $a\in A$ on the explicit complex represents the derived endomorphism induced by multiplication by $a$ on $K$; its cohomology is an actual $A$-module with this action. No flatness of $A/R$ or boundedness of $K,P$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, assertion that derived tensor cohomology is an algebra-module; expanded using section-derived-tensor-product, definition-derived-tor and lemma-flip-douoble-tensor-product.

proof.text: Apply [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor] to $R\to A$, $M=K$ and $E=P$. Thus $C^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}K^p\otimes_RP^q$ with $a(x\otimes y)=(ax)\otimes y$ and $d(x\otimes y)=d_Kx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Py$. This action respects the balanced relations because multiplication by $a$ on $K^p$ is $R$-linear. The differential is $A$-linear since $d_K$ is $A$-linear. Restriction to $R$ leaves precisely the same abelian groups, balanced relations, direct sums and differentials, giving a chain isomorphism $j_{K,P}:\operatorname{Res}_RC(K,P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}_RK\otimes_RP)$, identity on every symbol $x\otimes y$. For $f,h$ both induced total maps send that symbol to $f(x)\otimes h(y)$, so $j$ is natural in these chain maps.

source.place: Tag 06Y5, section-derived-base-change, the mixed total tensor construction preceding Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change).

proof.text: Work on the one-object site with only the identity covering and coefficient ring $R$. Sheaves of $R$-modules are literally $R$-modules: the sheaf condition imposes no relation, so sheafification is the identity and satisfies the additive sheafification hypotheses. The K-flatness test is exactly [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] with first input $L=\operatorname{Res}_RK$ and second input $P$. Its inverse lax tensorator gives a simultaneous natural comparison $\theta_{L,P}:Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_RP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RL\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_RP$ whenever $P$ is K-flat. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q_R\epsilon$ is invertible. Define, using ordinary right-to-left composition, $$\eta_{K,\epsilon}=(1_{Q_RL}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R\epsilon)\circ\theta_{L,P}\circ Q_R(j_{K,P}).$$ All three factors are isomorphisms. This uses K-flatness only for the given $R$-complex $P$, not for $K$ or for its restriction.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding K-flat construction; Tag 0FPT, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived; specialized to the one-object identity-cover site. Compare More on Algebra Tag 064M, definition-derived-tor.

proof.text: Put $L=\operatorname{Res}_RK$, $L\prime=\operatorname{Res}_RK\prime$, and $\bar f=\operatorname{Res}_Rf$. Naturality of the comparison in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] says $$\theta_{L\prime,P\prime}\circ Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(\bar f\otimes h)=(Q_R\bar f\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_Rh)\circ\theta_{L,P}.$$ Functoriality of localization gives $Q_R\epsilon\prime\circ Q_Rh=Q_R(g[0])\circ Q_R\epsilon$. Compose the displayed identity on the left with $1\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R\epsilon\prime$ and use bifunctoriality of derived tensor; then use the symbolwise naturality of $j$ proved in step 1. The result is exactly $$\eta_{K\prime,\epsilon\prime}\circ Q_R\operatorname{Res}_R\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes h)=(Q_R\bar f\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(g[0]))\circ\eta_{K,\epsilon}.$$ This proves the required square for every supplied $f,g,h$; $h$ need not be a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding K-flat construction; Tag 0FPT, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived; specialized to the one-object identity-cover site. Compare More on Algebra Tag 064M, definition-derived-tor.

proof.text: For $a\in A$, multiplication $\mu_a:K\to K$ is an $A$-linear chain map since $A$ is commutative. In step 3 take $f=\mu_a$, $h=1_P$, $g=1_N$ and the same augmentation. By the action formula of [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor], $\operatorname{Tot}(\mu_a\otimes1)$ is multiplication by $a$ on $C$. Hence $\eta$ identifies that endomorphism with $Q_R(\operatorname{Res}_R\mu_a)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}1$. Finally $d_C$ being $A$-linear makes both $\ker d_C^n$ and $\operatorname{im}d_C^{n-1}$ stable under $A$. Their quotient $H^n(C)$ is therefore an actual $A$-module with $a[z]=[az]$. The cohomology factorization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies its underlying $R$-module and these endomorphisms with the derived tensor cohomology through $\eta$. No step used flatness of $A/R$ or boundedness.
